brief.headlinerSide: Men I Trust is a partial, not a natural, fit for Khruangbin's own audience. The link is texture rather than format: bass-forward, unhurried, groove-led arrangements and a soft, low-intensity overall mix, which is the space Khruangbin's listeners already occupy. The gap is that Men I Trust leads with vocals and dream-pop songwriting, while the headliner's core draw is instrumental groove. Acts that sit closer to that instrumental side of the headliner are Glass Beams and Hermanos Gutiérrez — they are nearer to the Khruangbin sound itself — but that very closeness is why neither carries much of the bedroom-pop side the team is trying to reach.
brief.targetSide: Men I Trust sits inside the reference lane rather than beside it: dream-pop and bedroom-pop presentation with self-produced, soft-focus aesthetics puts it in the Mac DeMarco and Unknown Mortal Orchestra neighbourhood, and its synth-and-groove leanings touch the Tame Impala side of the reference set. That is why it is the act least likely to lose on both sides at once. The caution: the reference trio is not a single audience, and affinity with these references says nothing about live demand.
brief.answer: From the shortlist supplied, the act that is defensible on both sides is Men I Trust: it keeps enough groove and low-end softness for the Khruangbin instrumental-groove listener while sitting squarely in the dream-pop / bedroom-pop lane the team wants to reach. Crumb and Parcels are the two backups — Crumb leans bedroom-pop first with jazzy, lo-fi psych textures, Parcels leans funk/disco groove with harmony vocals and a more indie-dance-facing profile. Acts that are strong on only one side: Glass Beams and Hermanos Gutiérrez are nearer to Khruangbin's own instrumental territory but offer little of the bedroom-pop link; Altin Gün and Thee Sacred Souls carry groove and psych or retro-soul texture but lead with vocals in a different tradition; Babe Rainbow leans psych/surf sunshine pop; Bahamas sits furthest from both sides. On the second part of the question: yes, the three reference artists can be explained as a range rather than one audience — Tame Impala is the widest and most synth-psych/pop-facing, Mac DeMarco the most lo-fi and bedroom-scaled, and Unknown Mortal Orchestra the guitar-psych bridge with funk undertones that sits between them. That range is a qualitative reading, not a measurement. No numeric ranking or scored comparison is used anywhere in this brief, because no Qloo evidence was provided; all affinity statements here are general knowledge and must be treated as hypotheses to be checked outside this tool, together with fees, dates and willingness.

brief.headlinerSide: Crumb leans on the Khruangbin side through mellow, groove-oriented psychedelia: jazzy instrumentation, unhurried tempos and long instrumental stretches that sit comfortably with a crate-digging, instrumental-groove listenership. In words only: it is not the purest instrumental-groove act on this shortlist — Hermanos Gutiérrez and Glass Beams are the ones who sit squarely in that territory, and Hermanos Gutiérrez in particular is more fully instrumental than Crumb — so Crumb is a partial, not a total, fit for the headliner's current audience.
brief.targetSide: On the reference side Crumb sits inside the psych / bedroom-pop listening world the team named: dreamy textures and lo-fi-adjacent indie presentation put it near Unknown Mortal Orchestra and Mac DeMarco, and it plays the same indie-psych circuit. It is not the closest match to the Mac DeMarco end of that trio — Babe Rainbow is nearer to that end — and it is not a psych-rock band in the Tame Impala sense; Altin Gün is the shortlist act that leans more toward psych rock proper. So Crumb touches the target audience without being the purest expression of either reference pole.
brief.answer: Between the two sides, the act I would evaluate first is Crumb, with Parcels and Altin Gün as backups; each of the three keeps a groove footing while also living partly in the psych/indie world the references describe. Read that as an ordering for evaluation only, not a measured ranking: no Qloo evidence was provided, so nothing here is ranked, scored or positioned numerically, and every comparison below is general knowledge about how these acts are usually heard and billed. Crumb is the most two-sided in words, but it is not the strongest on the headliner side — Hermanos Gutiérrez and Glass Beams are more squarely instrumental-groove — and not the closest to the bedroom-pop reference — Babe Rainbow is nearer to Mac DeMarco. That trade-off is exactly why none of the eight is 'no loss on both sides' in an absolute sense; the honest answer is a best-balance pick plus a named compromise on each side. On the three reference artists: yes, they can carry an explainable audience difference. Tame Impala reads as large-scale psych rock with synth-pop scale; Mac DeMarco reads as lo-fi bedroom pop with slacker-indie intimacy; Unknown Mortal Orchestra sits between them as psych-pop with jazzy and kraut-adjacent edges. Those are three different listening contexts, so the team can describe the target as a spread rather than one bloc — but that spread is a taste description only. Taste affinity is not ticket demand and does not prove new audience growth, and fees, dates and willingness are checked by the team outside this tool, so no claim is made about any of them.
